groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: A person practicing or offering to practice registered, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing in the state shall submit evidence of qualification to practice and shall be licensed under t

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.quote: "board" means the Board of Nursing

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.quote: "board" means the Board of Nursing

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: "board" means the Board of Nursing

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.
Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.
Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: Completed a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board
example.quote: the applicant has successfully completed a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board
a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board

fields.meaning: The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

example.quote: the applicant has successfully completed a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.quote: a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

example.quote: the applicant has successfully completed a registered nurse education program accredited by a national nursing accrediting body and approved by the board

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)
e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'
Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Examination prescribed by the board for RN licensure

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.
Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.
Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

example.quote: A license to practice nursing may not be renewed unless the nurse has complied with continuing competence requirements established by the board by regulation.

The regulations must require that a licensee receive not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a lic
not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a license

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']

value: pain management and opioid use and addiction (2 hours, for APRN DEA holders)
example.quote: The regulations must require that a licensee receive not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a lic

fields.meaning: Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: The board may issue a license by endorsement to practice as a registered, advanced practice registered, or practical nurse, whichever is appropriate, to an applicant who has worked as a nurse within t

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Applicant must be licensed in another state and, in the board's opinion, meet Alaska qualifications. Applicants who have not worked as a nurse in the past five years must also meet continuing competency requirements or complete a board-approved course of study.
example.quote: The board may issue a license by endorsement to practice as a registered, advanced practice registered, or practical nurse, whichever is appropriate, to an applicant who has worked as a nurse within t

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: "board" means the Board of Nursing

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.
Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.
Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.quote: A person practicing or offering to practice registered, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing in the state shall submit evidence of qualification to practice and shall be licensed under t

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.quote: A person practicing or offering to practice registered, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing in the state shall submit evidence of qualification to practice and shall be licensed under t

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: practice or offer to practice nursing without a license, unless the person is practicing within the scope of a delegation properly made under AS 08.68.805 or is giving necessary aid to the ill, injure

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: use in connection with the person's name a designation that implies that the person is a licensed nurse unless the person is licensed

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: practice or offer to practice nursing without a license, unless the person is practicing within the scope of a delegation properly made under AS 08.68.805 or is giving necessary aid to the ill, injure

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'
One-line plain-English description

example.value: Obtained or attempted to obtain a license by fraud or deceit

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?
Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?
Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: practice of registered nursing means the performance for compensation or personal profit of acts of professional service that requires substantial specialized knowledge, judgment, and skill based on the principles of biological, physiological, behavioral, and sociological sciences in assessing and responding to the health needs of individuals, families, or communities
example.quote: "practice of registered nursing" means the performance for compensation or personal profit of acts of professional service that requires substantial specialized knowledge, judgment, and skill based on

fields.meaning: High-level methods, e.g. ['medical','surgical','mechanical']

value: assessment of problems, counseling, and teaching
administration, supervision, delegation, and evaluation of nursing practice
teaching others the skills of nursing
execution of a medical regimen as prescribed by a person authorized to practice medicine
performance of acts of medical diagnosis and prescription of medical therapeutic or corrective measures (under board regulations)
for APRN: performance of acts of medical diagnosis and the prescription and dispensing of medical, therapeutic, or corrective measures

certified clinical nurse specialist (CNS)

advanced practice registered nurse
licensed physician
licensed physician assistant
licensed dentist

fields.meaning: Whether certain advanced practice nurses (typically NPs and CNMs) must have a written collaborative practice agreement with a physician to practice or prescribe.
Whether the state provides a pathway for certain APRNs to practice fully independently without a physician collaboration or supervision requirement.
Number of supervised or collaborative practice hours required before an APRN may qualify for full independent practice authority.
Whether APRNs must obtain a separate board-issued certificate or number to prescribe or furnish drugs, beyond the basic APRN license.
The DEA controlled substance schedules that APRNs are authorized to prescribe, which may differ by role or state.
Statutory limits on opioid prescriptions issued by APRNs, including maximum day-supply and documentation requirements.

Whether APRNs with DEA numbers must register with the state's controlled substance prescription monitoring database.

example.quote: require that a licensed advanced practice registered nurse who has a federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number register with the controlled substance prescription database under AS 1

fields.meaning: Whether the state board maintains a registry of certified nurse aides, including disciplinary findings.

example.quote: The board shall maintain a registry of certified nurse aides.

fields.meaning: Whether the state has a separate certification category for medication assistants or medication assistive persons who may administer certain medications under nurse supervision.
Whether licensed nurses are explicitly authorized by statute to delegate nursing tasks to unlicensed assistive personnel under defined conditions.

example.quote: An employer may not discharge, threaten, or otherwise discriminate against a nurse employed by the employer regarding the nurse's compensation, terms, conditions, location, or privileges of employment

fields.meaning: Whether the state has enacted the Enhanced Nurse Licensure Compact (eNLC), allowing multistate licensure privileges.
Whether applicants may choose between a single-state license and a multistate license when applying for licensure.
Whether the state has a voluntary non-disciplinary alternative or diversion program for nurses impaired by substance use or mental health conditions.
